# pantoken

Instructure design tokens and icons, reshaped for every platform. pantoken resolves Instructure UI's
tokens and icons once into a canonical model, then emits many small, individually-publishable
packages — CSS, SCSS/Less/Stylus, React/Vue/Svelte, Tailwind/Panda, native Swift/Kotlin, WordPress,
Figma, and more — unified by an unscoped `pantoken` meta package.

Read `README.md` for the consumer quickstart. This file is the map to everything an agent needs; open
the linked docs only when a task calls for them.

## How to work here

- **Use the `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` CLIs — never raw pnpm, npm, or yarn.** They're global bins. Package
  scripts must never shell out to `pnpm` internally: CI provides `vp` but not `pnpm` on PATH, so a
  `pnpm run …` inside a script breaks the docs deploy. Details in `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md`.
- **Never kill a process you didn't start.** "Port in use" is not "stale" — the user runs their own
  dev servers in other windows. For your own preview server, bind a distinct port with `--strictPort`.
  If a port is taken, pick another or ask.
- **Decide one fork at a time.** Give a recommendation plus the tradeoff, then let the user choose.
  Verify third-party claims (upstream token names, browser support, a library's capability) before
  asserting them.
- **Writing:** active voice, contractions, plain language, Oxford comma. Don't use empowering,
  harnessing, unlocking, supercharging, transforming, game-changing, seamless, robust, leverage, or
  synergy.
- **Keep `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/web-components` runtime graphs Node-free** — they ship
  to the browser. A value import of a postcss-based `@cssdoc/*` package pulls a `node:module` shim
  into the bundle and kills client JS. Type-only imports are fine; value imports belong in build
  scripts and tests.
- **Generate a changeset for every user-visible change.** Run `pnpm changeset` and commit the
  `.changeset/*.md` file alongside the code change.
- **When refining user-facing packages, evaluate `@pantoken/ai` in the same change.** If package
  recommendations, CLI target examples, or usage conventions changed, update the consumer agent assets
  in `ai/pantoken-ai` so assistant guidance does not drift.
- **Keep security docs current.** When a code change alters a threat, adds a control, or closes a
  residual risk in `ASSURANCE.md`, update both `ASSURANCE.md` and `SECURITY.md` before merging.

## Knowledge map

| When you need to…                                                                  | Read…                                |
| ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| Understand the monorepo, the pipeline, and why `@pantoken/model` exists            | `docs/architecture/overview.md`      |
| Author or extend a component (records, the modifier convention, aliases, `@scope`) | `docs/conventions/authoring.md`      |
| Work on the web components (shadow CSS, `register()`/prefix, the JS-behavior tier) | `docs/conventions/web-components.md` |
| Run more than one theme or color scheme in a single document                       | `docs/conventions/scoping.md`        |
| Build, lint, release, or work on the docs site + i18n + cssdoc integration         | `docs/conventions/build-and-docs.md` |
| Avoid re-solving a known bug or gotcha                                             | `docs/engineering-log.md`            |
| Amend the security assurance case after adding a new input surface or control      | `ASSURANCE.md`, `SECURITY.md`        |
| Match an agent to a domain                                                         | `AGENTS.md`                          |

## Repo shape

Organized by _how you consume_ each package: `packages/` core machinery · `formats/` importable
serializations (css, icons, scss, components, …) · `platforms/` generated foreign-ecosystem source ·
`renderers/` UI integrations (web-components, framework wrappers, bridges) · `bundlers/` build-pipeline
plugins · `design/` Figma + swatches · `plugins/{pantoken,postcss,typedoc,vite}/` · `tools/` internal
build tooling · `ai/` consumer-facing agent assets. The gate is `pnpm run ready` +
`pnpm run check:publish`.

# Build, release, and the docs site

## Use the `vp` toolchain, never pnpm directly

- `vp` / `vpr` / `vpx` are **global** bins. Run tasks via `vp run <task>`, execute bins via `vp exec
  [-F <glob>] <bin>`.
- **Package scripts must never shell out to `pnpm`.** CI (`.github/workflows/docs.yml`) provides `vp`
  via `voidzero-dev/setup-vp` but **not** `pnpm` on PATH, so a `pnpm run …` inside any script breaks
  the docs deploy with `pnpm: command not found`. Local dev has pnpm, so a top-level `pnpm run X` is
  fine — but scripts it calls must stay pnpm-free internally.
- `.css` formatting: `vp fmt` (oxc) is JS/TS/JSON only and no-ops on `.css`. Stylelint owns core CSS
  correctness; cssdoc owns documentation comments. `lint:css` and `lint:cssdoc` run in `ready`, and
  both are wired into the `vite.config.ts` staged hook.

`vpr docs:dev` builds interactions before staging its browser bundles. The interactions build task
declares its workspace dependencies' builds as prerequisites, so `@pantoken/utils` is built even
when its `dist` output is missing. Run `vp run @pantoken/interactions#build` rather than invoking
`scripts/build-iife.ts` directly when prerequisites haven't been built.
CSS generation also declares both runtime and development workspace builds as prerequisites:
its generator imports `@pantoken/plugin-props-minify` from development dependencies. Keep these
prerequisites on the generator task so standalone generation and docs startup use the same order.

## Accessibility evidence in the docs build

The docs build keeps the checked-in evidence (`docs/public/accessibility/results.json`) current, so
the `## Accessibility` tables on each CSS API page match the code that ships. The `accessibility`
asset task (`docs/scripts/accessibility-refresh.ts`, run by `docs:assets`) fingerprints every audited
record from its CSS and examples, built stylesheet and behavior script, and the inputs every page
shares (tokens, base, focus, elevation, the automatica11y version, and the audit harness). It
re-audits only records whose fingerprint differs from the one stored in the snapshot and merges the
results back, so an unchanged tree is a fast no-op.

- `vp run @pantoken/docs#docs:accessibility` refreshes stale records. `--check` (via
  `docs:accessibility:check`) reports them without auditing; `--all` re-audits everything; `--adopt`
  stamps current fingerprints onto existing evidence when you know the inputs didn't change the results.
- Commit the updated snapshot with the change that caused it. The `component-accessibility` CI job
  re-audits stale records and fails when the committed snapshot differs.
- On CI (or with `DOCS_ACCESSIBILITY_INSTALL_BROWSER=1`) the refresh provisions the audit browser
  when it needs one. `docs:dev` sets `DOCS_ACCESSIBILITY_AUDIT=skip` so a dev server never starts an audit.
- The tables are raw HTML in the generated page. The segmenter classifies them as `audit` blocks, so
  their visible text (headings, pill labels, details) enters `l10n/docs.api.pot` through the normal API
  translation pipeline while markup and `<code>` selectors stay verbatim. The fixed labels live in
  `ACCESSIBILITY_AUDIT_STRINGS` in `docs/.vitepress/i18n.ts`.

## Local component accessibility reports

`vp run audit:components` is an explicit, uncached full audit task, separate from `ready` (the docs build re-audits only stale records; see above). It uses the
catalog-backed automatica11y development dependency, current local package builds, and authored
component examples. It doesn't send examples to a remote audit service.
The task first runs the shared `build:all` prerequisite, restoring the complete workspace build
graph in dependency order. A fresh checkout or restored CI task cache doesn't contain package
outputs until those tasks run; building only components, CSS, and interactions can leave their
build-time workspace dependencies missing.

The tool requires Chrome or Chromium. Check setup with
`vp exec -F @pantoken/components automatica11y doctor`. If a browser is missing, explicitly opt into
its download with `vp exec -F @pantoken/components automatica11y doctor --install-browser`.
Don't bypass an outdated-browser warning without understanding its effect on results.

Each run retains the tool's original Markdown and JSON reports and a coverage index in
`a11y-report/<run>/`. The command returns an error for infrastructure failures; accessibility
violations alone don't fail it. Keep axe and IBM findings separate, and read incomplete and
needs-review results rather than treating an empty violations list as a verdict.
The index separates explicit gaps/undetermined checks from coverage notices and lists tier
execution per target, archetype, and state. Notices preserve `outcome.coverage`, summary gaps,
and not-testable notes, with missing requested tiers derived when absent from the tool's outcome.
Notices can overlap explicit gap counts; they aren't unique defects, and the counts aren't additive.
Target completion doesn't mean every requested tier ran in every state. In automatica11y 0.11.0,
supplemental npm states run rules and simulated VSR only. Interaction, computed, and condition
checks run on fresh pages and are attached to the initial configuration. Missing supplemental tiers
remain visible limitations, not passes or infrastructure errors. Nested execution errors still fail
the command. Original reports stay unchanged.
The npm archetype suite retains its authored fixture mapping and local package tarballs alongside
the reports. These tarballs are test inputs, not release artifacts. Each theme/scheme case uses
the same semantic example. Keep the report's authored-fixture provenance and browser warnings.
Each npm report batch gets its own mapping; automatica11y rejects mapping entries for targets
outside that invocation.

The supported matrix has four combinations: rebrand light/dark, Canvas light, and Canvas High
Contrast light. Canvas themes don't support dark mode. Older raw reports retain their unsupported
Canvas dark cases as historical evidence; don't count those cases as supported product coverage.

### Results on component API pages

Generated component pages append the audit to the record's **Accessibility** section, without a
separate header, so it follows the authored `@accessibility` (or `@a11y`) guidance. The audit is
one table per tier (axe-core rules, conditions, interactions, computed styles) plus a simulated screen-reader
table. axe reports only failed and needs-review rules, so its table lists those rules with their
WCAG criteria; a listed rule with no finding in a column that ran axe shows Pass. IBM Equal Access
results aren't rendered because they don't align to WCAG. Rows are checks (name, then `WCAG 2.2` and the success criteria on a second line; the name
may wrap, pills never do); columns are the supported theme/scheme
pairs, and each cell is an `instui-pill` with an icon (Pass, Fail, Not applicable, or Review needed; missing or undetermined results always show the last so they're never read as passes). A check that's Not applicable in every column is omitted, and so is a table with no remaining rows.
A cell takes the worst result across the page and npm evidence for that column. A row that fails or
needs manual review spans two table rows: the label cell uses `rowspan="2"` and a second row spans
every theme column with the tool's explanation (columns with identical text share one paragraph).
Because Markdown tables can't span rows, the audit tables are raw HTML blocks with no blank lines
inside, escaped with `html()`; the segmenter preserves them verbatim, so their labels aren't
machine-translated. Every record
needs that tag; a record without one still gets a bare **Accessibility** section, but a test fails.
The docs build reads a checked-in snapshot at `docs/public/accessibility/results.json`; it doesn't
run a browser or select whichever local audit happens to be newest. A component without evidence
shows **Not audited**, including plugin components outside the core audit inventory.

name: Release

# Automated releases via the changesets action. On push to main:
#  - with pending changesets, it opens/updates a "Version Packages" PR (runs `changeset version` →
#    version bumps + per-package CHANGELOGs) and sets that PR to auto-merge. Merging the feature PR
#    is the human gate; the Version PR is derived entirely from changesets reviewed there, so the
#    required checks gate it rather than a second review;
#  - once that PR merges (no changesets left), it publishes the bumped packages to npm with provenance
#    (via `release:publish` → scripts/release/publish-npm.ts, the npm CLI) and cuts a GitHub release per
#    package from the script's `New tag:` stdout. That path also uploads a `docs-deploy-request`
#    artifact, which is what lets `docs.yml` publish the site for released versions only.
#
# Token-free npm auth: publishing uses npm OIDC "trusted publishing" (`id-token: write` + `npm publish`),
# not an `NPM_TOKEN`. Requires (one-time):
#  - repo Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions → "Allow GitHub Actions to create and
#    approve pull requests" (so the action can open the Version PR);
#  - repo Settings → General → "Allow auto-merge", plus at least one required status check on `main`
#    (the ruleset requires `ci-gate`, `changeset-gate`, and `codecov/patch`) — auto-merge needs
#    something to wait on, or the Version PR just sits there;
#  - a trusted publisher for EACH published package on npmjs.com (package → Settings → Trusted Publisher:
#    GitHub Actions, repo `thedannywahl/pantoken`, workflow `release.yml`). A package with no trusted
#    publisher 404s on publish; the script logs it and continues, so the rest still ship;
#  - a `RELEASE_PAT` secret: a fine-grained personal access token scoped to this repo with Contents:
#    read/write + Pull requests: read/write. The Version PR is opened (and its branch pushed) with this
#    token so CI runs on it automatically, and auto-merged with it so the merge commit triggers this
#    workflow's publish pass. PRs authored (or merges performed) by the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN don't
#    trigger workflows — their checks sit in `action_required` and need a manual click. The PAT is
#    git/PR auth only; it has nothing to do with npm publishing, which stays OIDC/token-free.

Contributor accessibility tooling runs trusted authored examples in a local browser, using
lockfile-pinned automatica11y and locally built styles and scripts. Its reports are advisory evidence,
not security controls or a WCAG certification. Fixtures must not contain credentials or private data.

The security-relevant assets are:

- The integrity of the source repository and release workflow.
- The integrity and provenance of published npm packages and GitHub releases.
- The correctness and reproducibility of the canonical token IR and generated outputs.
- The integrity of consumer files written by the CLI.
- The confidentiality of repository and release credentials.
- The availability of build, documentation, and transformation tools when processing expected inputs.
- The integrity of a consumer process that loads a Pantoken package or plugin.

or confidential application data.

# Security policy

## Supported versions

pantoken publishes many small packages from this monorepo, all versioned together. We support the
latest published release of each package. Fixes land on `main` and ship in the next release; we don't
backport to older lines.

## Security requirements and scope

pantoken is a design-token transformation and distribution system. It converts Instructure design tokens and icons into CSS, framework integrations, build-tool plugins, design-tool data, and generated platform source. It is not an authentication, authorization, cryptography, or application-security library.

### What users can expect

- Published downstream packages use a vendored, versioned token model and do not require consumers to retrieve the GitHub-hosted upstream design-token source.
- Generated output is reproducible from the repository source and pinned dependencies.
- Tokens Studio colour modifiers from the pinned upstream source are validated for structure,
  operation, colour space, numeric range, reference integrity, and colour type before publication.
  Malformed modifiers are recorded for review and block replacement of generated artifacts until an
  explicit rewrite is supplied.
- npm releases include provenance linking the package to its source commit and GitHub Actions workflow.
- The project tests token resolution, output generation, reference integrity, package exports, and supported integrations in continuous integration.
- Reported vulnerabilities affecting the latest release will be investigated and, when confirmed, fixed in a subsequent release.

 # Build, release, and the docs site
 
+## Generated values and translation identity
+
+Compatibility Markdown is formatted through `vite-plus/fmt` before it is written, so running
+`sync:compatibility` doesn't need a later table-format repair commit.
+
+Generated package compatibility paragraphs opt in with `<!-- pantoken-generated-values -->`.
+Their code spans and link destinations become stable `{{ptk_code_N}}` placeholders during
+extraction and lookup. Generated JS callouts use the same contract; authored descriptions,
+examples, and prose numbers don't opt in automatically. CSS value/code columns and HTML `<code>`
+content already stay outside translatable units.
+
+The compatibility page opts in at whole-file level. Its generated tables normalize padding before
+keying, and the **Current format** column treats numeric version metadata as bindings while keeping
+its explanatory words translatable. Status, limitations, reasons, new rows, and grammatical changes
+still need translations. Generated API templates include a stable page scope so existing translations
+with different wording aren't merged just because their machine values differ.
+
+After generating English API pages, migrate existing catalogs without invoking a provider:

# Formatter-stable releases and generated-value localization

## Problem and evidence

Compatibility updates currently embed machine-owned data in translation identity:

- `scripts/release/compatibility.ts::renderMarkdown` emits literal values into
  `docs/compatibility.md`, which `docs.guides` catalogs as one whole-file message.
- `docs/scripts/write-api-compatibility.ts` embeds versions, formats, and environments in
  API prose units. `refresh-api-pot.ts`, `translation-memory.ts`, and
  `check-locale-drift.ts` currently use those literal units.
- The compatibility generator emits compact tables. A stdin-only reproduction confirmed
  that `vp fmt` pads those tables and changes separator widths. Markdownlint already
  disables `table-column-style`; this is not a reason to disable more checks.
- Release publishing deliberately runs `gate:i18n`. Keep that gate, its locale policy,
  and normal translation requirements intact.

Recorded intent from compatibility commit `962c640f0`: show supported floors and the current
format on package pages, preserve the normal i18n pipeline, and handle translations separately.
The current failure mechanism above is inferred from inspected source and the formatter reproduction.

## Agreed approach and scope

Use stable placeholders for explicitly identified machine-owned fragments, then substitute
current values after translation lookup. Apply the mechanism across generated documentation,
not only compatibility pages. No AI translation run is part of this implementation.

Keep actual values in machine-readable manifests and readable rendered documentation.
Do not globally strip numbers, normalize prose, mask entire support claims, weaken drift
policy, exempt release commits, or introduce a browser runtime dependency.

Extend the Markdown primitives in `tools/translation-adapters`, reusing the existing
mask/restore and template-token conventions rather than creating a second translation cache.

- Provide an explicit, namespaced marker for generated fragments with stable logical keys.
  Separate a canonical translation template from its current value bindings.
- Translate/cache the template, then restore bindings into each document or unit separately.
  Identical templates may share a translation without sharing values.
- Validate unknown, missing, duplicated, conflicting, or corrupted placeholders. Permit
  translator reordering without losing binding identity or occurrence counts.
- Treat bindings as text/Markdown data with context-appropriate escaping, never executable
  expressions or unrestricted object-path lookups.
- Canonicalize formatting only within explicitly generated regions before deriving template
  identity, so table padding caused by changed values cannot invalidate whole-file messages.
  Preserve authored prose and its meaningful whitespace.

- Preserve the direct-Node/no-nested-`vp` constraint in docs orchestration.

### 3. Adopt the contract across generated documentation

Inventory generated translatable units, then mark every machine-owned fragment that can
currently churn their keys. Reuse existing preserved segments where already sufficient.

Primary producers and boundaries:

- Compatibility matrix and package support sections: upstream ranges/resolved refs,

- `tools/i18n-engine/src/pipeline.ts` content extraction, catalog matching, rendering, and

Formatter stability is independent of the shared placeholder implementation.
